title: Deadlock with tokio 1.7.0
notes: Runtime shutdown drops a task from inside a waker call while h2 holds its streams mutex; the task's Drop re-locks it -> deadlock. Maintainers reproduced; fixed in tokio#3870 (scheduler shouldn't shut down tasks already on the runtime). holder=runtime: the problem is scheduler drop re-entrancy. injectable=no: runtime-internal, and Dropwise does not count shutdown drops.

title: Make update API cancel safe
notes: Merged fix: a client disconnect dropped the update future partway through the fan-out to local/remote shards, so only some replicas applied the update (inconsistency between nodes). Fix spawns the critical section. Remote requests already sent keep running (outlives=yes). Found by review; no failure reported.

title: make simple source cancel safe
notes: Merged fix without a description. Timestamper::tick() = sleep(tick_duration) + write-lock + send Progress; it was recreated on every select! loop iteration, so a busy source keeps resetting the sleep and progress can stall. The consequence is my inference from the code; the fix is the evidence. Medium confidence.

title: Queue-proxifying a local shard can drop the shard if the transfer future is cancelled after `local.take()`
notes: Label 'accepted' plus a whitebox reproducer test in the issue. local.take() and then an await: cancel_on_token (select!) drops the future while it owns the LocalShard, leaving replica_set.local=None. The shard is owned only by the dropped future (holder).

title: bug: AsyncSinker can mark finish complete before awaited on_finish work completes
notes: Fixed by the merged #20021. called_on_finish is set before on_finish().await; if the process future is dropped mid-finish, the sinker's Drop fallback sees the flag and skips on_finish, so the commit/cleanup is lost. The progress is a flag in the outliving sinker (shared_object); bookkeeping says done but it was not delivered.

title: sync: fix possible dangling pointer in semaphore
notes: tokio batch_semaphore: an acquire future dropped after its waiter was split into the notify list dangles; the test added in the PR segfaults on master. Wait-queue machinery -> runtime. Found by code reasoning, confirmed by a test. injectable=no: runtime-internal memory safety needs loom-level interleavings.

title: bug: HTTP pagination retry can lose a spilled result page if request is cancelled during restore
notes: Fixed by the merged #20016. try_take_page pops a spilled page from the queue, then awaits restore(); if the request future is dropped there, the page is neither in the queue nor in last_page, so retrying the page loses it. The popped page is owned by the dropped future.

title: proxy http cancellation safety
notes: Merged fix plus a regression test: hyper drops the request handler on client disconnect, but the SQL query keeps running on Postgres; a retry of the insert then hits a duplicate key. Fix: spawn the handler and cancel via a token on connection drop. injectable=yes with an in-process fake backend that keeps executing (medium). phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: proxy_instance_serial_ws() uses `select!` with non-cancel-safe future(s)
notes: Maintainer confirmed and fixed in omicron#3411 and propolis#435/#447, with a playground reproducer for SinkExt::send. select! drops the send future holding the item, or recv() after it has pulled a message from ws_stream, so console bytes are lost. Found by an audit of select! uses.

title: fix(aws_s3 source): complete in-flight SQS message processing before shutdown
notes: Open PR with regression tests (inflight_processing_completes_despite_shutdown); the linked #24010 reports duplicates on scale-down. The shutdown signal wins the select! over run_once() after events went to sinks but before the SQS delete, so messages are redelivered. cancel_source=select (the shutdown signal is a select! branch). Not merged -> medium.

title: fix(log-store): ensure cancellation safety for log reader next_item call
notes: Merged fix, reviewer 'good catch'. The kafka sink selects next_item() against the delivery future; next_item has popped a flushed item and is reading its chunk from storage when it is dropped, so the item is lost. Fix buffers the read future in the reader.

title: Subrequest response finish can lose the terminal Done task if cancelled under channel backpressure
notes: Open, no maintainer reply, but a runnable whitebox tokio test is in the issue (audit). finish() sets BodyMode::Complete before awaiting tx.send(Done); a cancel under backpressure drops Done and a retried finish() is a no-op. The progress is recorded in the outliving BodyWriter -> shared_object.

title: fix(storage): Move timeout layer before to ensure cancel safety
notes: Merged bug-fix PR with little detail: the timeout layer sat outside RuntimeLayer, so a timeout dropped only the waiter while the op kept running on the IO-runtime task and the retry layer re-entered it. Mechanism inferred from the diff and the 'reentrant after timeout' wording -> low confidence. injectable=unknown: depends on opendal backend behaviour. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: Cancelling a hashless asset download can persist and reuse an incomplete cache entry
notes: Runnable whitebox reproducer in the issue; maintainer judged it low priority, reporter closed it, fix PRs not merged. Ctrl-C aborts the owner and the JoinSet drop aborts the download mid-write, leaving a truncated file at the canonical cache path that a later run accepts when there is no sha256.

title: connection: wake 'stopped' streams on stream finish events
notes: Merged fix, maintainer 'great catch'. A Stopped future polled once and then dropped left its waker in the connection's stopped map until the connection closed; memory grew on long-lived connections (seen in anemo). Waker-list machinery -> runtime. injectable=unknown: the leak is visible only in quinn-internal state.

title: cluster: avoid accidentally dropping TimelyContainer
notes: Merged fix for an incident. ClusterClient takes TimelyContainer out of the shared Arc and awaits a channel; a gRPC client disconnect drops it, and the container's Drop blocks on Timely workers forever, wedging a tokio thread. The taken container is owned by the dropped future.

title: `tokio::sync::Mutex` appears to be acquired multiple times without being released
notes: Closed not_planned: the maintainer diagnosed the user's select! cancelling read() mid read_exact. Bytes already consumed into the dropped buffer desync the framing and the server panics on invalid data. The defect is in the reporter's code (app). A runnable reproducer is in the issue.

title: pageserver management API doesn't poll request handlers to completion if client hangs up [P:1] [S:1]
notes: Maintainers confirmed; fixed by #4314 (shield handlers in spawned tasks). A client hang-up drops the detach handler after the tenant moved to Stopping, so the tenant stays Stopping and later detach requests fail; prod issues mentioned. The stuck state lives in the outliving tenant object.

title: Streaming partial cache reads can treat a cancelled cache writer as clean EOF
notes: Labelled 'bug'; a collaborator agreed with the proposed semantics and the issue has a whitebox test (audit). A cancelled miss-handler writer drops before finish(); an already-attached partial reader sees Ok(None), so a truncated body is served as complete to another request. The unfinished admission is owned by the dropped writer.

title: stdin: first line intermittently lost from Deno.stdin.readable on Unix (orphaned cancelled blocking read)
notes: Filed by a deno member with a minimal proof program. Cancelling the stdin readable drops the op future (deno CancelHandle, hence cancel_source=other), but the spawn_blocking read(0) stays parked, consumes the next line and discards it. Deno is a runtime -> library. The blocking pool is covered by Dropwise settling. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: H2→H2 proxy: downstream RST_STREAM is not observed while the upstream request-body write is blocked, pinning connection-window credit indefinitely
notes: A downstream RST_STREAM is not observed because the select! arm body awaits an upstream write; the stream handles are held (not dropped), pinning window credit. No future is destroyed (the fix adds a cancellation) -> adjacent. Fixed in b79ce4f / #977.

title: Handle `Stream` dropped before end-of-stream flag sent
notes: codebook-gap: the dropped thing is an h2 SendStream handle, not a future (typically dropped with the future or task that owns it). Dropping it before EOS left the stream open and the peer hung; fixed in h2#210 (send RST_STREAM CANCEL on drop). Stream state lives in the shared connection. Medium confidence.

title: Keep consensus operation awaiters alive for concurrent waiters
notes: Merged PR with 4 regression tests verified to fail before. When a waiter's timeout dropped its recv, cleanup removed the shared broadcast entry, dropping the sender and failing the other waiters of the still-in-flight op (which then applied); timed-out batch awaiters leaked. The consensus op keeps running -> outlives=yes.

title: RTCache lookup cancellation can leave same-key requests blocked on a stale coalescing lock
notes: Labelled 'bug', whitebox repro in the issue (audit); fix PR #948 open. RTCache::get inserts a zero-permit CacheLock into the shared lockers map, then awaits lookup(); a cancel skips cleanup, so later same-key readers wait forever (no lock_timeout).

title: server serial task's send-to-listeners future is not cancel-safe
notes: Reported by an Oxide engineer who observed duplicated serial output. When another select! branch wins, the send-to-listeners future may already have delivered to some listeners but cur_output is not cleared, so the next iteration resends; the ws.next() + send path can also lose messages. Open, but the maintainer observed it.

title: `try_join_all` can drop a shard worker-restart future after workers are stopped, leaving the local shard update handler stopped
notes: Labelled 'bug' and fixed by the merged #9671. try_join_all drops a sibling on_optimizer_config_update future after wait_workers_stops() took the pending update receiver but before run_workers(); the shard's update pipeline stays stopped. The taken receiver is owned by the dropped future.

title: storage-controller: retains futures during recv
notes: Merged hotfix (pulled into v0.112.2). Instance::recv rebuilt select_all(r.recv()) on every poll and dropped it at the end of the poll, so a cancel-safe recv that yields before returning never completes (starvation). Retaining the FuturesUnordered fixes it.

title: lru: future cancellation or not polled will lead to deadlock
notes: Labelled type/bug, fixed by the merged #3911 with an explicit drop(future_1) scenario: the first lookup_dedup caller owns the in-flight fetch and others wait on the shared entry; dropping it leaves the waiters stuck forever. A later comment says the deadlock seen in prod was the not-polled variant (adjacent), but the cancel case was fixed.

title: Spawn a task to run services_ensure
notes: Merged fix for observed #3098. A client timeout closes the socket and dropshot drops services_ensure mid-way, leaving zones partially configured and missing from existing_zones (state behind a mutex); the next PUT re-brings the same zone up and fails.

title: fix(iroh-gossip): connection loop misuses `tokio::select!` leading to read errors
notes: Merged fix: select! over read_message (length prefix, then body) could abort mid-message; the next read took body bytes as a length, causing random connection drops. The partial-read position lives in the dropped future. iroh-gossip is a published crate -> library.

title: [proxy]: BatchQueue::call is not cancel safe - make it directly cancellation aware
notes: Merged fix linked to an internal cloud issue. When the batch leader's call() is cancelled after get_batch() removed the other callers' jobs from the queue, those jobs' responses are never sent and the followers fail. The removed batch is owned by the leader's dropped future.

title: pageserver: Flush op dropped on shutdown due to canceling ListWriter
notes: Shutdown cancels a CancellationToken before flushing; ListWriter's loop observes the token and exits, dropping the queued flush op (ERROR 'dropped flush op'). The loop stops by token check; no future is destroyed mid-await -> adjacent (cooperative cancellation). Closed as no longer reproducible, no explicit fix.

title: node:http retries an explicitly destroyed POST on a reused connection
notes: codebook-gap: JavaScript-level cancellation in deno's node:http polyfill; req.destroy() does not stop canRetryRequest() from resending the POST on a reused socket, so the server gets a duplicate. Runnable repro; fix PR open. No Rust future is destroyed, so it is out of scope for yes and labelled adjacent.

title: Add test for broken WAL delta after stream records abort
notes: Merged test plus fix (#7791). Updates during a stream-records transfer bump the receiver's last-seen clocks; aborting the transfer leaves clocks claiming more than was transferred, and a later WAL-delta transfer skips the gap, corrupting the replica. The clocks are bookkeeping in the outliving shard. injectable yes but heavy (multi-peer), low confidence.

title: file descriptor leak
notes: Maintainer confirmed the mechanism (no fix possible): timeout drops a tokio::fs read, but the blocking read on a device file never returns, so File's drop waits and the fd is never closed; fds accumulate until opens time out. Maintainer says the app should use AsyncFd -> app. injectable=unknown: needs a device that blocks forever. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: Avoid sending new messages before connection finishes
notes: Merged follow-up cancel-safety fix: a reconnect cancelled partway left the client partially connected while send() still delivered commands, so commands meant for the old cluster reached the new one and crashed it. The fix records the 'reconnecting' state. cancel_source not explicit (probably a select! in the controller loop) -> medium.

title: layer: evict downloaded-but-not-initialized
notes: Labelled t/bug, fixed by the merged #7030. get_or_maybe_download cancelled after the download (in a spawned task) but before initializing LayerInner leaves the layer file on disk while in-memory state says not resident: disk leak, and keep_resident stalls on downloads.

title: Corrupt connections
notes: A collaborator confirmed it and there is a runnable repro (poll once, drop, then PING returns the stale GET value). A timeout drops query_async after the request was written but before the reply was read; the reply stays in the reused aio::Connection and is paired with the next command. The resolution is to use MultiplexedConnection.

title: No-op ALTER SINK can restart KV log reader without rewind and panic
notes: User-observed panic, fixed by the merged #26412 and #26484. A no-op UpdateConfig wins the select! and cancels consume_log_and_sink without rewinding the KV log reader; the next sinker calls start_from() on a non-Reset reader -> panic. The reader outlives the future.

title: ClickHouse sink checkpoint cancellation can drop insert finalization ownership before log truncation
notes: Only evidence is the reporter's whitebox test (audit); no maintainer reply. barrier(true) does inserter.take() then awaits end(); if the rebuild select! branch wins, the finalizer is dropped before log truncation, so replay may duplicate or diverge from what ClickHouse applied. injectable=unknown: the outcome depends on ClickHouse's handling of an unfinished insert. Low confidence.

title: The first terminal event is ignored after using `stdin`
notes: Maintainer confirmed a known, documented limitation: timeout drops a tokio stdin read, but the spawn_blocking read keeps running and consumes the next keypress, so the first terminal event is lost. App misuse of tokio stdin for interactive input. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: Cancelled search requests remain in SearchQueue and can cause spurious TooManySearchRequests
notes: Labelled bug (by Linear sync), whitebox test in the issue, fix PR open. A cancelled request drops its oneshot receiver after its Sender went to the scheduler task, which keeps the closed sender in its queue; the stale entry counts toward capacity and can get live requests rejected with TooManySearchRequests. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: core/: Report pending connection being aborted
notes: Aborting a pending connection removes the pool entry first, so the task's later 'aborted' event finds no entry and is dropped instead of reported (fixed in #2517). The abort is signalled by dropping a notifier, which the task observes and exits cooperatively; the defect is lost event bookkeeping, not state lost by a destroyed future.

title: [bootstrap-agent] Make destructive endpoints cancel-safe and interlocked
notes: A maintainer's PR to make bootstrap-agent endpoints cancel-safe against client disconnects (spawn plus interlock); closed unmerged by the author ('incorrect in at least a couple ways'). No concrete failure, reproduction or merged fix in this thread.

title: Add a oneshot to notify the profiles daemon if the stream is dropped
notes: Merged fix for linkerd2#2523 (memory leak). When a service's profile Rx stream is dropped from the router cache, the spawned daemon future and its gRPC stream live on until the next update, so streams accumulate. Fix: a oneshot hangup notifies the daemon.

title: [persist] Fix a futurelock in the recent update lease attempt (#34980)
notes: Merge commit of PR #34980 (persist update-lease futurelock fix, database-issues#10081). The PR has more evidence (discussion, reproducer) and is primary; it is labelled adjacent (futurelock).

title: [wicketd] make installinator_progress cancel safe
notes: Merged; in review a maintainer found that cancelling report_progress after the RunningUpdate state advanced (possibly to Closed) but before the report was sent loses the report, while shared state says it was handled. Fixed with an unbounded channel and a std Mutex (no await while holding state).

title: Issue with graceful shutdown, cancellation tokens, and hanging eternally (possibly with lost wakers).
notes: Graceful-shutdown hang with CancellationToken; the reporter could not make a minimal repro and closed the issue within 20 minutes with no maintainer diagnosis. Whether a cancelled future is involved cannot be established.

title: Prevent basic_scheduler from panicking if a task is aborted from another thread
notes: Merged fix for #3662: JoinHandle::abort() from a thread outside the basic_scheduler panicked with 'scheduler context missing' when releasing the task. Scheduler-internal -> runtime. injectable=no: Dropwise drops targets and does not model cross-thread abort in scheduler internals.

title: storage: abort sink task when dataflow is dropped
notes: Merged fix for incident #56: dropping a sink dataflow did not stop determine_sink_resume_upper's spawn_blocking Kafka scan (abort has no effect on blocking tasks); with sinks restarting, scans piled up and caused OOM. Fixed with a cancellation token checked by the blocking task. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: Async-truncate sinks can lose delivery futures when cancellation happens during capacity backpressure
notes: Only evidence is the reporter's whitebox test (audit); no maintainer reply. After Kafka send_result() accepted a record, add_future_may_await awaits an older popped delivery before registering the new one; if the rebuild select! branch wins, both delivery futures are dropped unregistered, so replay resends -> duplicates. Low confidence.

title: [support bundle] Monitor for cancellation without accidental task-blocking
notes: Fixes #9259 (Nexus API timeouts): select! polled &mut collection and awaited a DB call in another arm's body while collection held pool access -> futurelock (a future alive but not polled). adjacent.

title: fix(mysql-cdc): use connection pool to avoid data loss caused by unsafe cancellation
notes: Merged critical fix with a timeout repro: dropping mysql_async exec_drop mid-query leaves the connection mid-protocol; later reads on it return empty/EOF, so backfill thinks the snapshot is done -> data loss. Fix uses a pool. injectable=unknown: needs a MySQL server or a protocol-faithful fake.

title: make `read_exact_at` cancel-safe
notes: Merged: dropping read_exact_at while the io_uring read was in flight would drop the FileGuard and let the kernel use a closed/reused fd (use-after-close); an interim scopeguard aborted the process instead. Fix passes the FileGuard into the uring op. Observable violation before the fix: process abort (panic); the underlying hazard is memory safety. injectable=unknown: kernel io_uring timing. phase=committed_unowned: the operation was irrevocably handed off (kernel/blocking pool/remote/other task) and completes with no owner (codebook example: late fd, consumed byte).

title: fix(walreceiver): Timeline::shutdown can leave a dangling handle_walreceiver_connection tokio task
notes: Merged fix for #7062: during Timeline shutdown, select! against shutdown_watcher dropped connection_manager_loop_step inside drop_old_connection, leaving a handle_walreceiver_connection task running after shutdown. Fix replaces cancel-by-drop with a CancellationToken.

title: H2 response-header timeout can drop the only ResponseFuture and make the session panic on retry
notes: Labelled bug/Accepted, fixed in 6dcc236. read_response_header takes resp_fut out of the session and awaits it under read_timeout; a timeout drops the only ResponseFuture, leaving the session with resp_fut=None, and a retried read panics.

title: page_service: `throttle()` is not actually cancel-safe (low impact)
notes: A maintainer states throttle() is not cancel-safe: dropping it between the accounting points leaves accounted_started and accounted_finished out of balance. Labelled t/bug; closed not_planned (low impact). Evidence is the maintainer's statement only -> medium.

title: Cancelled io-uring open futures leak fds
notes: Security report with a runnable PoC (fd count 7 -> 136), fixed by tokio. Dropping a polled io-uring open future marks the op Cancelled, and the later CQE's fd is discarded without closing -> fd leak. Real-time settling + an fd-count after_settle check could show it (needs an io_uring-enabled kernel).

title: Leakage of futures with pending notification on runtime drop
notes: Maintainers confirmed (runnable PoC); fixed via threadpool 'impl Drop for Queue' (#649). On runtime drop, a spawned future with a pending notification was leaked without running Drop, so tokio-signal could not detect the dead driver and deadlocked. Scheduler-internal. injectable=no: Dropwise does not count runtime-shutdown drops.

title: Task dropped in wrong thread when aborting LocalSet task
notes: I-unsound, fixed in #3934 (RUSTSEC-2021-0072). JoinHandle::abort on an idle LocalSet task drops the future on the aborting thread, so a !Send value is dropped on another thread. Scheduler-internal. injectable=no.

title: prevent select!-correctness problems for simple sources
notes: Unmerged earlier PR about the same defect as #12714: select! drops the timestamper tick() future mid-sleep (the interval can grow arbitrarily) or mid-send (progress lost). The merged #12714 is primary (stronger evidence).

title: compute: make `SequentialHydration::recv` cancel safe
notes: Merged fix for 'a previously unreported bug': SequentialHydration::recv may call GenericClient::send (not cancel-safe) while scheduling dataflows, so cancelling recv can drop a half-sent command. Fix moves sends to a forwarder task.

title: `tokio::select` with async ConnectionManager and channel for cancelation
notes: Several users report dangling connections or reading the same stream entry twice when xread_options loses a select!. A collaborator says the call is cancel-safe and the expectations are wrong (the request was already sent); one report stems from the deprecated aio::Connection (see redis-rs#325). Closed not_planned; no single confirmed defect.

title: Memory leak when futures are canceled
notes: A cancelled select! branch leaves a waker clone held elsewhere, keeping the whole task allocation alive (20GB/day leak). The maintainer calls this intended behaviour of the task allocation; the component that holds wakers forever is not identified. Closed not_planned.

title: bug: Stage Lance COPY can leave target data files without a manifest after query cancellation
notes: Fixed by the merged #20050. The async processor future loses the select against the finish notify after target Lance data files were written but before their fragments were recorded or the manifest published, so data files are left visible without a manifest.

title: propolis-cli may have a cancel-unsafe `tokio::select!`
notes: Follow-up of omicron#3356: the same InstanceSerialConsoleHelper::recv cancel-unsafety (message pulled from ws_stream, then lost at a later await), here in propolis-cli's select!. Fixed by propolis#435, which also resolves the recv part of #3356.

title: Dropping HTTP/2 response future doesn't cancel request body send and does not send RST_STREAM
notes: Fixed by the merged #4042; the issue has a runnable test. When the response future is dropped (timeout), send_task completes but the independently spawned pipe_task keeps the SendStream, so no RST_STREAM is sent and the stream keeps holding flow-control capacity, back-pressuring other streams on the connection.

title: S3 streaming multipart uploads can be leaked when a cancelled uploader is dropped after multipart upload starts
notes: Only evidence is the reporter's whitebox test with a fake S3 client (audit); no maintainer reply. After CreateMultipartUpload the upload_id lives only in S3StreamingUploader; aborting a compaction worker drops the uploader without AbortMultipartUpload, leaking the multipart upload and its parts on S3. Low confidence.

title: Cancelled shard snapshot recovery can leave a false dirty marker and load a healthy local shard as dummy after restart
notes: Fixed by the merged #9686. The recovery persists the shard initializing marker and then checks the cancellation token, returning Cancelled with a false dirty marker left behind. The early return is a cooperative token check, not a destroyed future -> adjacent (the unmerged #9773 also guards the drop path).

title: fix: phase-guard pattern for cancel-safe shard snapshot recovery
notes: Unmerged alternative fix (RAII phase guard) for the same false-dirty-marker defect as #9668, which was fixed by #9686. #9668 is primary.

title: fix(ext/http): don't panic on stream responses in cancelled requests
notes: Merged fix for #20315/#20298: when a TCP connection is force-closed, hyper drops the request future, which drops the body resource while the OpState lock is held -> panic. Deno is a runtime -> library. injectable=unknown: needs Deno's JS/op machinery.

title: `tokio::io::simplex` read/write data not equality
notes: Closed not_planned: the maintainer explained the user's select! of read_exact/write_all. write_all partially writes PATTERN, is cancelled, and the next write_all starts over, so the stream has a duplicated prefix and the reader sees misaligned data. Documented cancel-unsafety; the defect is in the user code (app).

title: Hyper returns a partial byte array when its runtime is closed mid-read
notes: Maintainer-confirmed with a runnable repro, fixed by #4069. Dropping the runtime that drives the HTTP/1 dispatcher drops the body Sender mid-body; the receiver treats it as a clean close, so a truncated body is returned as Ok (panics in SlateDB). The dispatcher future can also be dropped via ctx.target.

title: sync: wake mpsc receiver when a queued `reserve[_many]` returns permits
notes: Merged, with tests that fail before the fix. A cancelled or failed reserve_many returns partially acquired permits to the semaphore without waking a receiver blocked on a closed, idle channel, so recv() hangs. Permit machinery -> runtime. A Dropwise scenario that drops reserve_many and checks that recv returns None is feasible.

title: Fix cancelled snapshot recovery dirty marker
notes: Merged fix (#9686) for the false-dirty-marker defect reported in #9668; the maintainer closed #9668 citing this PR. The issue is primary (equal evidence).

title: fix(iroh): get rid of flume channels
notes: External reproducer (flume-bug-reproducer): cancelling a flume recv_async in select! loses the wakeup notification (not the message), so an actor whose only event source is the channel stalls until another send. iroh replaced flume (#2539 merged). Defect is in flume's waker machinery -> runtime/library.

title: Cleanup cancelled optimized segment
notes: Merged. Optimization stopped via the 'stopped' flag (graceful, cooperative cancellation) left a renamed optimized segment directory on disk. No future is destroyed; the early return comes from check_process_stopped -> adjacent.

title: net: call CancelIoEx on NamedPipeServer drop
notes: Proposed Drop calling CancelIoEx on NamedPipeServer to avoid an IOCP leak / use-after-free on the OVERLAPPED when pending I/O is dropped; closed by the author after the maintainer asked why not in mio (the mio PR is also closed). No reproduction, confirmation or merged fix.

title: persist: make Pending cancel safe
notes: Merged fix with a test that panics before it. block_until_ready mem::replaced the state with a Blocking placeholder, then awaited the taken JoinHandle; if dropped there, the placeholder stays and later into_result panics ('block_until_ready cancelled?'), aborting the process. The spawned write keeps running (outlives).

title: sled agent hung
notes: Sled-agent hang: the trust-quorum connection loop spun (infinite read loop) without yielding and starved the runtime; fixed by #9612 (infinite read loop / tokio hang). Futurelock was suspected but not confirmed; no cancellation involved.

title: persist/pubsub: fix connection leak on gRPC stream error
notes: Merged fix for database-issues#11276 (repro in the issue). On a gRPC stream error the reconnect loop drops the tonic Channel, but hyper's background task keeps polling the never-ending broadcast stream, so the HTTP/2 connection stays open: one leaked connection per reconnect. Fix: a cancel oneshot selected inside the stream.

title: tokio::process::Command leaves zombies when child future is dropped
notes: Maintainer-confirmed known limitation with a playground repro; addressed by #2907 (orphan reaping) and docs (#2952). Dropping a Child future with kill_on_drop kills the process but never waitpid()s it, leaving a zombie until another child is polled. Real-time settling + a zombie check could show it.

title: bug: Fuse mutation aggregation can lose commit metadata after cancellable object writes
notes: Fixed by the merged #20043. The async processor future loses the select against the finish notify after TableMutationAggregator::on_finish wrote segments/blocks but before CommitMeta was emitted (called_on_finish was already set), leaving orphaned storage objects with no commit or accounting.

title: LocalSet drop impl panics when dropped with unfinished futures
notes: Fixed by #1843 (maintainer). Dropping a LocalSet that still held unfinished futures panicked ('tasks should only be completed locally') instead of dropping them. Scheduler-internal. injectable=no: Dropwise does not model LocalSet/runtime drop.

title: Abort pending blocking search tasks when we drop/invalidate the search
notes: Merged critical fix (labelled bug). Dropping an invalidated or timed-out search dropped only the JoinHandles; queued spawn_blocking searches still ran, holding segments for over an hour ('Removing proxy segment which is still in use'). Fix: AbortOnDropHandle.

title: Cooperative shutdown in support bundles
notes: Merged, motivated by an observed CI flake (#10063): support-bundle collection was stopped by cancelling its future while tokio::fs writes were in flight on the blocking pool, so writes landed after the Utf8TempDir was dropped and cleanup failed. Replaced with cooperative cancellation. The cancel mechanism (select! on the collection future, per #9268) is inferred -> medium.

title: Shard snapshot transfer cancellation can leave source-side transfer snapshots behind
notes: A maintainer applied accepted/parked after first failing to reproduce; the source already has a TODO for this window, and the reporter's whitebox test shows it. After create_shard_snapshot finishes, cancelling the transfer (cancel_on_token select!) before the TempPath guard exists leaves the .snapshot and checksum on disk. Medium confidence.

title: proxy_h2: acknowledge downstream RST_STREAM while the upstream request-body write is blocked
notes: Fix PR for pingora#910 (downstream RST_STREAM not observed while the upstream write is blocked); landed via #977. The issue is primary (labelled adjacent).

title: select! with I/O read branch blocks program from exit
notes: Maintainers confirmed: select! drops a tokio stdin read, but its spawn_blocking read keeps running and runtime shutdown waits for it, so the program cannot exit until Enter is pressed. Documented and tracked in #2466. The blocking pool is covered by Dropwise settling.

title: StarRocks sink can lose transaction rollback ownership if checkpoint commit is cancelled during prepare or commit
notes: Only evidence is the reporter's whitebox test with a mock StarRocks server (audit); no maintainer reply. barrier(true) takes curr_txn_label, then awaits prepare/commit; if the consume future is dropped there, Drop/abort cannot roll back (label gone), leaving an external transaction orphaned and replay ambiguous. Low confidence.

title: fix: possible page_service hang on cancel
notes: Fixes #5341 (page_service hang on cancel): framed.shutdown() at the end of the connection handler was not raced with the shutdown watcher, so shutdown could hang; the fix adds a select! plus cancel-safety notes. The defect is a missing cancellation point (not a destroyed future losing state) -> adjacent.

title: network/sync: Fix justification response lost on peer disconnect
notes: Open PR with a regression test (response_after_disconnect_is_accepted) for #5414, filed by a Parity maintainer. On a sync-peer disconnect, pending_responses.remove_all() drops the in-flight justification response future, so a valid response from the request-response protocol is lost. sc-network-sync is a library crate. Not merged -> medium.

title: h2 debug assertion failed after future cancellation
notes: An h2 debug assertion fired after the runtime was dropped on SIGINT; the reporter later said the cancelled future was detached and never reproduced it. Closed not_planned as not actionable. Cause not established.

title: [persist] Update leases, take 2
notes: Persist update-lease change whose first version had a futurelock (RFD 609), fixed here with a reproducer (database-issues#10081). A future kept alive but not polled -> adjacent. Primary row for commit b8f9449 (the same change).

title: Break from deferred points wait when caller times out
notes: Merged. On a client timeout LocalShard::update drops the feedback oneshot receiver, but the sequential update worker keeps waiting in wait_for_deferred_points_ready, blocking all later updates on the shard (head-of-line). Fix checks sender.is_closed().

title: HTTP2 requests waiting an outstanding connecting task should not be canceled when the connecting task is canceled
notes: Maintainer agreed; runnable test in the issue; fix PR open. The shared connecting task is driven by the first request's ResponseFuture; dropping that future cancels the connect, and other requests waiting on the same connection fail with Canceled. Matches the codebook's 'shared connecting task owned by one request' (dropped_future).

title: fix: possible page_service hang on cancel (#5696)
notes: Merge commit of neon#5696 (page_service hang on cancel), the primary row (labelled adjacent).

title: Meta: hummock timer task panics during shutdown when a child loop is cancelled, tripping CI's `panicked at` check
notes: CI flake, fixed by the merged #26221. On shutdown, shutdown_background() aborts the detached child timer loops; the supervisor's unbiased select! can see the child's JoinError::Cancelled before the shutdown signal and panics. injectable=unknown: the trigger is runtime shutdown abort, which Dropwise does not count.

title: fix(storage): fix panics caused by merge iter future cancellation
notes: Merged fix for #6972 ('we experienced many bugs'): cancelling the merge iterator next() future dropped a live PeekMut, whose Drop re-sifts the heap and calls key() on an iterator in an intermediate state -> panic. Fix: a guard that pops instead.

title: Strange issue with tokio::select and MultiplexedConnection
notes: Collaborators explained the reporter's repro: select! cancels xread_options(BLOCK 0) but the request was already sent, so the server keeps the multiplexed connection blocked and later commands on it stall. The library calls this correct; the defect is in the app. injectable=unknown: depends on Redis server blocking semantics.

title: fix server leaking IO resources
notes: Unmerged external PR: dropping the axum::serve future leaves spawned per-connection tasks holding TcpStreams, so the port stays busy. The author says the implementation was wrong; there is no maintainer response, and whether this is a defect or intended detached-task design is not established.

title: fix(iroh-relay): do not use spawn_blocking in stun handler
notes: Merged removal of spawn_blocking from the STUN handler because blocking threads (not abortable) seemed to accumulate memory; the author notes the threads should expire after keep-alive and the cause is unclear ('some unintended lingering'). Cancellation is not shown to be the trigger.

title: tonic/client: support immediate cancellation of streams without sending End-of-Stream
notes: Feature PR: adds a CancellationHandle so tonic client streams can be aborted with RST_STREAM(CANCEL) instead of ending with EOS. The motivation is a missing cancellation API (a completing request stream always sends EOS); no dropped future causes a defect here.

title: Fix case where cancelled future would be leaked and add a regression …
notes: Merged fix with a regression test for #3964 (a regression from #3934): JoinHandle::abort() followed by an immediate drop of the handle did not drop the cancelled future until much later, so its resources leaked. Task-harness internal -> runtime. injectable=no: abort semantics are inside the scheduler.

title: Remove spurious `debug_assert` in `Counts::drop`
notes: Proposal to delete debug_assert!(!has_streams()) in Counts::drop, which fires when an h2 connection is dropped with open streams (e.g. a cancelled task); closed not_planned by the author with no maintainer input or reproduction.

title: Internal `grpc-timeout` can cancel receiver shard initialization after `local.take()`, leaving the target replica without a local shard slot
notes: Labelled bug/accepted by maintainers; fix PR #9770 with a regression test. init_empty_local_shard() does local.take(), then awaits stop/clear/build; tonic's server-side grpc-timeout drops the future and leaves the replica's local slot None. A separate function from qdrant#9665 (queue_proxify_local).

title: Tokio select! Macro Issue with Barrier
notes: Maintainer confirmed that Barrier::wait is not cancel-safe (fixing it would be breaking); documented in #6494. Dropping wait() in select! after registering still counts the arrival, so the next wait double-counts and the barrier releases extra times. Barrier is a codebook shared_object example.

title: Split `Controller::recv` into `ready` and `process`
notes: Merged fix for database-issues#3585 (private repo, not readable): Controller::recv, used as a select! branch in the coordinator loop, did cancel-unsafe processing after receiving a response, so a dropped recv could lose it. Split into a cancel-safe ready() and process(). Consequence (loss) inferred -> medium.

title: tap: fix tap response streams never ending
notes: Tap response streams never ended because the events sender moved into the Tap struct, which outlives the Dispatch future that was expected to close the channel. A channel-ownership bug (fixed by #299); the Dispatch drop at the limit is normal teardown, not a cancellation losing in-flight state.
